A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChroKnowledge work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluations on ChroKnowBench and ChroKnowPrompt experiments, including temporal performance, changed-object analyses, and span ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds Llama-3.1-70B evaluations and more complete model-by-year results.

M1.justification: The knowledge categorization, majority-vote object selection, backward and forward prompting, and distractor-generation procedures are unchanged in Sections 2 and 6 and Algorithms 1–2. Evaluating another model does not alter the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five domains, underlying data sources, temporal ranges, dynamic/static distinctions, and Generation, MCQA, and TF tasks. The additional biomedical heatmap reports an already evaluated domain.

E2.justification: V3 adds Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct to the model comparisons. Its expanded appendix heatmaps also include Llama-2, Llama-3, Gemma, MPT, Pythia, and Nemotron, which appeared elsewhere in v2 but were absent from its Figure 10 comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4 adds a 70B model configuration to the existing evaluation suite, extending the tested model scale. The reported dataset sizes, 10% prompting test subset, templates, matching criteria, and decoding temperatures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 5–7 extend the changed-versus-unchanged object analysis and previous-versus-total temporal span ablations to Llama-3.1-70B. These add evidence for existing analytical questions without introducing a new robustness condition or ablation design.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five exemplar combinations and the fixed-seed inference statement. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V3 adds 70B scores and previously unshown model-by-year results while retaining existing model rows in Tables 5–7. Figure 7 revises several gains: GPT4o-mini's general-domain dynamic unchanged-object gain changes from 6.3 to 7.0, matching Table 5 in both versions. Section 7.1 also updates domain averages alongside the expanded model set; these are not established same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical categorization rules in Table 1, temporal definitions, and algorithmic formulations are retained. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs absent from the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark, categorization framework, prompting contribution, and claims about benefits and challenges. Updated improvement percentages change the reported evidence without redefining the core claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning domain and template dependence, temporal cutoffs, adjacent temporal context, and difficulties with changing objects and unstructured legal data remain the same. Section 9 and Appendix A.9 retain their limitations and proposed need for complementary parametric techniques.

D1.justification: The implementation and access information remains unchanged, including vLLM, BFloat16, eight 80GB A100 GPUs, fuzzy-matching details, prompt templates, and the dataset/code availability statement. No additional reproduction instructions accompany the larger model.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to knowledge editing and temporal knowledge graphs are retained. Reference changes supply missing years, author information, and publication details for existing citations.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized revisions to the experimental setup, results prose, Appendix A.1.1, and figure references, and updates affiliations and the publication header. The section organization and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is broadly revised. Figure 1 becomes a six-panel domain/state overview; result plots receive additional model rows, curves, and revised labels or legends. V2's combined Figure 10 becomes three expanded domain heatmaps in v3 Figures 10–12, the subsequent radar figures are redrawn, and Table 6 is relocated.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly strengthens empirical support by testing a substantially larger open model in the existing evaluations and ablations. Expanded heatmaps expose previously omitted temporal profiles, and the redesigned overview better explains the categorization. Reporting remains imperfect: the new 70B biomedical static gain is 8.5 in Figure 7 but 8.7 in Table 5. The overall gain is useful but limited.
